plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy. Since the winner pays the second-highest bid (not their own bid), bidding higher than my value risks overpaying, and bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. With a value of $15, I should bid exactly $15 to maximize expected profit regardless of what the other bidders do.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy since you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid. This holds regardless of the number of competitors or their strategies, as it maximizes expected profit: bidding higher risks overpaying if you win, while bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions. With a value of $36, I will bid exactly $36 to ensure optimal expected earnings.

In a second-price (Vickrey) auction with independent private values, bidding one's true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of bidders or their strategies. This is because the payment depends only on the second-highest bid, not your own bid, so overbidding risks overpaying and underbidding risks losing profitable wins. With a value of $42, I should bid exactly $42 to maximize expected profit.
